content.text:
The prompt.md is old unrelated content (a prior task example). The repo is a playground. Task is "Create a game like minecraft". We should build a polished voxel sandbox game with Three.js.

Plan:
- Use Vite + Three.js (default-start supports vite).
- Implement voxel world with chunk meshing (greedy or simple face culling), procedural terrain with noise, block breaking/placing, player physics (walk, jump, gravity, collision), pointer lock for desktop, touch controls for mobile, hotbar, block types with textures (procedural canvas textures or generated atlas), day/night? Keep performance good.
- Should look nice: fog, sky gradient, ambient occlusion baked into vertex colors, water, trees, clouds.
- Sound? Maybe simple synthesized sounds via WebAudio (nice touch).
- UI: title screen with play, settings, controls; hotbar; crosshair; FPS; pause menu.
- Save world to localStorage maybe.
- Need to capture screenshots via playwright-cli and inspect. Must actually verify visually.

Let's think about scope and time. Building a Minecraft-like game is substantial. I'll write carefully modular code but maybe a single main.js ~1500 lines plus texture generation. Could split into modules: noise.js, world.js, mesher.js, player.js, textures.js, main.js.

Key technical design:

World: chunked, 16x16 columns, height maybe 64. Store blocks in Uint8Array per chunk (16*16*64 = 16384). Infinite-ish world generated around player with chunks loaded/unloaded in radius. Use seeded noise for terrain.

Block types: air, grass, dirt, stone, sand, water, wood(log), leaves, planks, glass, brick, snow? Keep 10.

Meshing: For each chunk, iterate blocks; for each visible face (neighbor transparent), add quad with texture atlas UVs and per-vertex AO + face shading. Build BufferGeometry with positions, normals, uvs, colors, index. Use a texture atlas generated on canvas: 16x16 tiles per block face type, NearestFilter, sRGB. Or use array of separate textures with material per block? Atlas simpler: one material, one draw call per chunk. Use MeshLambertMaterial? Better custom ShaderMaterial? Use MeshStandardMaterial with vertexColors and map, roughness 1. Lighting from directional + ambient. But face shading baked into vertex colors plus AO gives nice look. Standard material with vertexColors multiplies texture.

Water: separate transparent mesh with animated slight offset? Could use separate geometry with transparent material and opacity 0.75, no collision (or swim). Simplify: water is solid-ish but player can walk? Minecraft swims. Maybe water blocks with reduced gravity? Keep water non-collidable but allow walking through with slower movement and swimming. Hmm collisions: treat water as non-solid, apply buoyancy/slower speed. That's nice.

Terrain: fBm noise for height, biome-ish variation; trees on grass; flowers? Add sand near water level. Water fills below sea level. Caves maybe skip for performance. Add ores? Maybe not.

Meshing AO: compute standard voxel AO from 3 neighbors per corner. Add smooth lighting. Good visual quality.

Player: capsule-ish AABB 0.6x1.8, eye height 1.62. Movement with acceleration, friction, sprint, jump, gravity. Collision via sampling voxels around AABB. Pointer lock mouse look, touch joystick + drag look + jump button.

Raycast for block targeting: DDA voxel raycast up to 6 blocks; highlight selected block with wireframe box; break on left click/ tap? Mobile: tap to place? Better mobile controls: joystick, look drag, jump, and buttons for break/place maybe "mine" button toggles? Simplest: on mobile, tap on block breaks? But dragging to look conflicts. Could have two buttons: dig/place at crosshair. Add buttons with icons. Or hold screen to mine, tap place? Use UI buttons: "⛏" and "▣" acting on crosshair target. That's usable.

Desktop: WASD, space jump, shift sprint, mouse look, left click break, right click place, 1-9 hotbar, scroll wheel, F for fly? Creative flying toggle double-space? Keep fly toggle with F and Shift descend. Nice.

Save: localStorage of modified blocks? Could be complex; maybe save world seed and modifications map keyed by coordinates. Doable: map of edited blocks. Load on start. Also day/night cycle maybe. Keep a fixed nice sunset lighting? Day/night cycle adds charm: sun moves, sky color changes, ambient. Could implement with time of day and updating sky/fog/lights. Night maybe dark. Add stars? Perhaps keep a slow cycle with "golden hour" look default.

Performance: Render distance 5 chunks (radius) => 11x11 = 121 chunks, each maybe ~5k tris. Need to be careful generating on main thread causing hitches. Use incremental chunk building queue: build 1-2 chunks per frame. Mesh in main thread okay if optimized. Chunk gen 16x16x64 with 3D noise might be heavy. Use heightmap 2D noise, fill columns. Height 64, sea level 26. Terrain amplitude ~12. Trees.

Memory: 121 chunks * 16k = 2MB fine.

Maybe use larger chunk 16, height 64. Meshing arrays: preallocate arrays and push.

Also need to include nice textures. Procedural canvas textures with noise/dithering. Generate 16x16 pixel-art textures per block face (grass top, grass side, dirt, stone, sand, log side, log top, leaves, planks, water, glass, brick, snow, cobble?). Draw with random speckles seeded. Use atlas of 16x16 tiles at 16px each = 256px. Add mipmaps? With atlas mipmaps bleeding across tiles; use padding or NearestFilter with generateMipmaps false. Pixel look is fine but at distance aliasing. Use mipmaps with 4px padding per tile? Simpler: use texture atlas with each tile 32px and 2px padding, generate mipmaps maybe. Hmm, to avoid bleeding, use NearestFilter and no mipmaps; distances will shimmer. Could use a texture array? Three.js DataArrayTexture with sampler2DArray requires custom shader. Could do custom ShaderMaterial with array texture, fog, lighting. That's more work but gives crisp mipmapping. Alternative: individual texture per block face and merge geometry per material — many draw calls per chunk (12 materials * 121 chunks = too many).

Atlas with padding: tile size 32, pad 4 on each side replicating edge; UVs inset. Mipmaps will bleed from padding but padding replicates so it's okay until very low mip levels. Could generate mipmaps manually? Three's generateMipmaps on canvas texture uses WebGL; padding helps. Use minFilter LinearMipmapLinear, magFilter Nearest for crisp pixel look; anisotropy 4. With 32px tiles + 4 pad, fine.

Actually simpler: NearestFilter, no mipmaps, and add fog to hide distant shimmer. Minecraft-ish. Let's use mipmaps with padding for quality.

Let's design atlas: TILE=32, PAD=4 => cell 40. 4x4 grid = 160x160? Need maybe 14 textures. Use 4 columns x 4 rows. Texture names list index. We'll generate pixel art procedurally with deterministic RNG.

Block definition:
0 air
1 grass (top grass, side grass_side, bottom dirt)
2 dirt
3 stone
4 sand
5 water
6 log (top log_top, side log_side)
7 leaves
8 planks
9 glass
10 brick
11 snow? maybe snow block
12 cobblestone
13 glowstone? maybe lantern emitting light? Skip light.
Add "bedrock" at bottom.

Faces: order +X, -X, +Y(top), -Y(bottom), +Z, -Z.

AO calculation standard: for each face corner, check side1, side2, corner occupancy; ao = 3 - (side1+side2+ (side1&&side2?1:corner))? Standard formula: if side1 && side2 -> 0 else 3 - (side1+side2+corner). Vertex color shade multiplied.

Face shading: top 1.0, sides 0.8/0.72, bottom 0.55.

Sky: Use gradient shader sphere or scene.background color + fog. Better: large sky dome with ShaderMaterial gradient (horizon warm, zenith blue) and sun disc sprite. Clouds: a layer of white blocky clouds (instanced boxes or a plane with texture) at y=90, slow drift. Use simple white semi-transparent boxes generated as merged geometry. Nice.

Sun: directional light + lens-y sprite? Use a bright circle in sky shader maybe. Add sun position based on time; lighting changes.

Environment: fog color matches horizon.

Water: transparent blue with vertex wave animation? Use shader modification via onBeforeCompile maybe. Simpler: material with transparent, opacity 0.8, color blue, and animate UV via map offset? Texture is atlas, offset would break. Could use separate water texture material with normal-ish pattern and animate map offset. Water blocks separate geometry per chunk with a water material (transparent). Animate a subtle vertical bob by updating mesh position? Eh. Keep static water but with animated caustic texture using canvas? Could animate texture offset if water uses own texture (not atlas). That's doable: water texture 32x32 blue pattern, wrap repeat; set material.map.offset over time. Nice.

Underwater: tint overlay when camera in water; reduce fog distance.

Selection outline: LineSegments box around target block.

Could it be that the mesh's geometry is actually the held block geometry? No, chunk mesh created in world.meshChunk with solid geometry. But `buildChunkGeometry` uses `pushQuad` with positions... Wait in `pushQuad`, I do:

```js
positions.push(v[0], v[1] + offset, v[2]);
```
where v = face.verts[i]. For solid faces, verts are 0/1 values! I forgot to add the block x,y,z coordinates to the face vertex positions. Indeed! In `buildChunkGeometry`, I pass face.verts directly without adding x,y,z. So all quads are at the same unit cube, overlapping. That's why terrain is a mess: all faces of all blocks are stacked at 0..1 within each chunk, and mesh position only offsets by chunk origin. The gray plane etc.

The `offset` param currently used as water top offset but pushQuad not used for water. Remove offset or keep.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a polished browser game like Minecraft ("BLOCKFALL") in the PlayGround repo.

## Requirements
- User request: "Create a game like minecraft" (single broad request; no further constraints given).
- Must work on desktop and mobile browsers with touch controls.
- Must be visually verified with Playwright screenshots and inspected, rejecting blank/loading scenes.

## Decisions
- Built with Vite + Three.js (r0.170.0), no external assets; textures generated procedurally on canvas.
- Chunked voxel world (16×16×72), procedural terrain/trees/water, greedy-ish face culling with baked AO and face shading.
- Single atlas material for solid blocks (`alphaTest` for leaves/glass); separate animated water texture/material.
- Game features: mining/placing, hotbar, held block, particle bursts, synthesized WebAudio sounds, day/night cycle, clouds, sky shader, save to localStorage, pause/menu/loading UI, desktop pointer lock, mobile joystick/look/mine/place/jump.
- Software renderer detection disables shadows and caps pixel ratio for Playwright/SwiftShader captures.

## Work State
### Completed
- Project scaffolding (`package.json`, `index.html`, `src/style.css`, modules), npm install, Vite build passes.
- Core world/mesher/player/environment/input/audio/effects/UI implemented.
- Fixed critical mesher bug: solid quad vertices were not offset by block `x,y,z`, causing all terrain stacked into unit cubes; added `origin` to `pushQuad`.
- Fixed `Input` crash (`mineButton is not defined`) by storing `this.mineButton/placeButton/jumpButton`.
- Verified game renders terrain, trees, water, sky, HUD via Playwright.
- Improved terrain formula to produce mountains/oceans (~20% water) and snow peaks.
- Reduced title overflow; resized/repositioned held block; moved hint above toast.
- Added debug access `window.blockfall` with `state`/`target` getters.

### Active
- Rewriting `World.findSpawn()` to pick an open, flat, scenic spawn with an open view direction and water in mid-distance; it now returns `{x,z,h,score,yaw}`. Last edit applied but not yet built/tested.
- Menu camera still needs replacing with a guaranteed aerial view along the spawn's scenic yaw.
- Need to update `main.js` to use `spawn.yaw` instead of `world.scenicYaw(...)` for initial and fallback spawn.
- Held block still slightly too large/low; consider size ~0.15 at z≈-0.8.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Update `main.js` spawn calls to use `spawn.yaw ?? world.scenicYaw(...)` in both initial spawn and invalid-saved-position fallback.
2. Replace `updateMenuCamera()` with an aerial camera above spawn (e.g., `player.y + 26`, raised above local terrain) looking ~70 blocks along the scenic yaw at `y+2`, with subtle sway.
3. Adjust held block to ~0.15 size at `(0.33,-0.28,-0.8)` and update its animation base position.
4. Wait for Vite rebuild, run `node /tmp/opencode/inspect.mjs`, and inspect `screenshots/inspect-menu.png` / `inspect-game.png`.
5. Iterate on spawn quality/open vista until screenshots show open terrain with water/land/mountains, not a terrace wall.
6. Run `./capture.sh` with `CAPTURE_URL=http://localhost:3002 CAPTURE_DIR=screenshots CAPTURE_START_SELECTOR='#play-btn'` to verify desktop + mobile.
7. Test gameplay interactions (mine/place, hotbar, pause/resume, mobile controls) and check console errors; fix any issues.
8. Update README if desired and ensure production build passes.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: state machine, camera, interaction, HUD, boot, save.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js`: terrain height, spawn/scenic selection, chunks, raycast, persistence.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/mesher.js`: chunk/block geometry, AO, face shading, water geometry.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/textures.js`: procedural atlas/icons/water texture.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/blocks.js`: block registry, hotbar, opacity/solidity.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/player.js`: FPS physics/collision/camera.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/environment.js`: sky shader, sun/moon/stars, fog, clouds, lighting.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/input.js`: keyboard/mouse/pointer lock/touch controls.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/style.css`: full UI styling/responsive/mobile.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: markup for menu/HUD/loading/pause/touch controls.
- `/tmp/opencode/inspect.mjs`: Playwright script logging world/player state and taking menu/game screenshots.
- `/tmp/opencode/debug.mjs`: top-down/high-view debug screenshots.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/`: latest captures (`inspect-menu.png`, `inspect-game.png`, `final-desktop.png`, `final-mobile.png`).
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/dist/`: Vite build output served by runtime.
- `/tmp/blockfall-server.log`: server log; server runs in tmux session `blockfall` on port 3002.

## Important Context
- Dev server: tmux session `blockfall` runs `PORT=3002 node $RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-start.mjs`; it auto-rebuilds via Vite watch. Check log for build errors.
- Playwright CLI's bundled browser path mismatch (`chromium-1243` missing) means `playwright-cli open` fails; use custom Node scripts with runtime Playwright config (`~/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json`) instead. `capture.sh` works.
- Playwright runs SwiftShader CPU rendering; FPS ~20 at 1440×900 is expected, not hardware failure.
- Current menu background problem: camera was placed inside/behind uphill terraced terrain; use aerial camera.
- Current game spawn problem: player can face a wall of 1-block terraces; new spawn algorithm requires flatness (`maxH-minH <= 4` over 8-block area), land ratio ≥ 0.5, and selects the most open scenic direction.
- Water is non-solid; `getBlock` returns `AIR` for unloaded chunks and `BEDROCK` for y<0.
- Leaves are `opaque:false` with special-case same-block culling; glass similar; solid faces adjacent to water are now rendered.
- Water geometry uses absolute world coords with mesh at origin; solid geometry uses local coords with mesh positioned at chunk origin.
- Save key: `blockfall.save.v1`; mute key: `blockfall.muted`. Save stores seed, edits, time, player position/yaw/pitch.
- Title button text is exactly "Play" so capture auto-start can click it.
